fact: The health ministry's e-Santé strategy states that the ministry has a Système National d'Information Sanitaire under its Direction des Statistiques, covering the whole country for the reporting of health data; the stocktake behind it was validated in September 2018.

The Stratégie Nationale E-Santé 2019-2023 carries project P121, strengthening and extension of the SNIS, in an action plan of 15 projects costed at USD 10 million (CFA 5,690,500,000) over five years, with funding still to be mobilised.

The strategy says the SNIS reports health data nationwide by electronic, semi-electronic and manual means, and that DHIS2, online since September 2016, has begun to be deployed in health facilities for data entry, in 'certain' facilities only.

The strategy gives no count of facilities entering data in DHIS2, saying only that deployment has begun in certain health facilities; it counts 1,026 integrated health centres and 2,443 health huts in the public network.
The strategy states that there is not yet a national electronic patient record project, only a few initiatives under way, and its 15-project action plan for 2019-2023 lists none.
The only electronic patient record activity the strategy reports is the digitalisation of two health districts, Gaya and Gothèye, of 72 districts; it gives no facility count.
